title.en: Don't Let Anyone Trap You with Rules!

body.en: Paul gives a warning that protects believers from a sneaky trap: don't let anyone judge you by what you eat or drink, or by religious festivals and special days. Why? Because these things were only SHADOWS of what was coming — and the substance, the real thing those shadows pointed to, is CHRIST. Imagine seeing a shadow of a tree on the ground, then walking around to see the actual tree, tall and real — why would you keep staring at the shadow once you've found the tree? Paul also warns about people who seem extra spiritual — claiming special visions, worshipping angels, taking pride in false humility — but who have actually lost connection to the Head, which is Christ! It's like a hand disconnected from the body: it might look impressive on its own for a moment, but without connection to the Head, there is no real life or growth. Paul even warns against rules that sound very holy — 'don't touch this, don't taste that' — rules made up by humans that have no power at all to stop sinful desires. True holiness was never about a list of human-made rules. It is about staying connected to Christ, the Head, who alone gives life, growth, and real victory over sin.

verse.en: These are a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ.

label.en: Activity sheet: Don't Let Anyone Trap You with Rules!

body.en:
Big idea: holiness is relational connection to Christ, not human-manufactured rule-keeping — a vital, often-missed nuance. Paul's warning here is not against holy living (which the rest of Colossians strongly affirms) but against confusing genuine holiness with legalistic substitutes: dietary rules, religious calendars, mystical experiences, and self-imposed asceticism that "have the appearance of wisdom" but no power over the sinful nature (2:23).

The image of being connected to "the Head" (2:19) is crucial: spiritual life, growth, and victory over sin flow from real, living connection to Christ — not from a checklist. This protects children early from two opposite errors: thinking holiness is achieved by following enough rules, or thinking rules don't matter at all. The truth is neither — genuine holiness is the fruit of staying close to Christ, the Head, from whom all real growth comes.

Conversation starters: (1) Can you think of a "shadow" — something that pointed forward to Jesus before He came? (2) What is the difference between a rule that helps you stay close to Jesus and a rule that just makes you feel impressively religious? (3) Why do man-made rules have "no power" against sinful desires, according to Paul?

Pray together, asking God for hearts that stay genuinely connected to Christ rather than satisfied with outward religious performance.
